section: Vishnukundins - political history, Madhava Varma I and II
subsections: Capitals and their shifts (Indrapalanagara, Amarapura, Denduluru, Bezawada) → ruler
Sequence of post-Ikshvaku dynasties - correct order Ikshvakus → Brihatpalayanas → Salankayanas → Vishnukundins

accepted.s: Which of the following was regarded as the first capital of the Vishnukundins?
accepted.x: Amarapura was the first capital of the Vishnukundins. The rulers referred to themselves as Amarapurishulu.
accepted.tq: Use direct capital–dynasty identification.
accepted.sec: Capitals and their shifts (Indrapalanagara, Amarapura, Denduluru, Bezawada) → ruler  [APPSC]

accepted.s: Amarapura, associated with the Vishnukundins, has been identified with which place?
accepted.x: Amarapura has been identified with Munnanuru in the Amrabad area of Nagarkurnool. Yaga-vedikas were found there.
accepted.tq: Distinguish similar capital locations by matching the place with its identification.
accepted.sec: Capitals and their shifts (Indrapalanagara, Amarapura, Denduluru, Bezawada) → ruler  [APPSC]

accepted.s: Who suggested that Amarapura should be identified with Velpuru in Guntur?
accepted.x: B.S.L. Hanumantha Rao identified Amarapura with Velpuru in Guntur, whereas another identification places it at Munnanuru.
accepted.tq: Test the scholar–interpretation association directly.
accepted.sec: Capitals and their shifts (Indrapalanagara, Amarapura, Denduluru, Bezawada) → ruler  [APPSC]

accepted.s: Indrapalanagara, also known as Sukrapuram, is identified with which place?
accepted.x: Indrapalanagara or Sukrapuram is identified with Tummalagudem in present-day Yadadri-Bhuvanagiri district of Telangana.
accepted.tq: Discriminate between closely associated Vishnukundin capital locations.
accepted.sec: Capitals and their shifts (Indrapalanagara, Amarapura, Denduluru, Bezawada) → ruler  [APPSC]

accepted.s: Indrapalanagara was built by which Vishnukundin ruler?
accepted.x: Founder Indravarma built Indrapalanagara, as recorded in the Tummalagudem inscription.
accepted.tq: Apply the ruler–construction association; beware of swapping rulers with similar names.
accepted.sec: Capitals and their shifts (Indrapalanagara, Amarapura, Denduluru, Bezawada) → ruler  [APPSC]

accepted.s:
Consider the following statements:
1. Indrapalanagara was the capital of Madhava Varma I.
2. Indrapalanagara was the capital of Govinda Varma.
3. Indrapalanagara has been identified with Tummalagudem.
Which of the statements given above are correct?
accepted.x: All three statements are correct. Indrapalanagara served as the capital of Madhava Varma I and Govinda Varma and is identified with Tummalagudem.
accepted.tq: Check whether the same capital is linked with multiple rulers and a specific location.
accepted.sec: Capitals and their shifts (Indrapalanagara, Amarapura, Denduluru) → ruler  [APPSC]

accepted.s: Which Vishnukundin ruler moved the capital from Amarapuri to Denduluru?
accepted.x: Madhava Varma II shifted the capital from Amarapuri to Denduluru because of constant Pallava wars and fortified Amarapuri.
accepted.tq: Use the capital-shift clue to identify the ruler.
accepted.sec: Capitals and their shifts (Indrapalanagara, Amarapura, Denduluru, Bezawada) → ruler  [APPSC]

accepted.s: Denduluru, the later capital of the Vishnukundins, was situated near which ancient centre?
accepted.x: Denduluru, also called Dendulurapura, was situated near Vengi or Pedavegi in Eluru district.
accepted.tq: Match the capital with its geographical setting.
accepted.sec: Capitals and their shifts (Indrapalanagara, Amarapura, Denduluru, Bezawada) → ruler  [APPSC]

accepted.s: After acquiring the Krishna region, the Vishnukundins used which place as a capital for some time?
accepted.x: Bezawada, or Vijayawada, was used as a capital for a period after the Vishnukundins acquired the Krishna region.
accepted.tq: Identify the temporary capital from the territorial-expansion context.
accepted.sec: Capitals and their shifts (Indrapalanagara, Amarapura, Denduluru, Bezawada) → ruler  [APPSC]

accepted.s: The Indrakeeladri and Mogalrajapuram caves are associated with the Vishnukundin occupation of which place?
accepted.x: The Vishnukundins carved the Indrakeeladri and Mogalrajapuram caves at Bezawada, present-day Vijayawada.
accepted.tq: Link monuments to the correct capital or regional centre.
accepted.sec: Capitals and their shifts (Indrapalanagara, Amarapura, Denduluru, Bezawada) → ruler  [APPSC]

accepted.s: Which one of the following is NOT listed as an additional capital or possible early centre of the Vishnukundins?
accepted.x: Keesaragutta, Vinukonda and Puranisangamam are listed as additional capitals or centres. Vijayapuri was the capital of the Ikshvakus, not an additional Vishnukundin capital in this list.
accepted.tq: Find the location belonging to a neighbouring dynasty rather than the stated group.
accepted.sec: Capitals and their shifts (Indrapalanagara, Amarapura, Denduluru, Bezawada) → ruler  [APPSC]

accepted.s: Which title is most specifically associated with Madhava Varma II?
accepted.x: Madhava Varma II bore the title Janasraya. Shadabhigna belonged to Govinda Varma, Mahakavi to Vikramendra Varma I, and Sakala Bhuvana Rakshabharanaikashraya to Vikramendra Varma II.
accepted.tq: Use a title–ruler match and separate similar royal epithets.
accepted.sec: Titles → ruler (Janasraya, Trikuta-Malayadhipati)  [APPSC]

accepted.s: The title Trikuta-Malayadhipati was connected with the conquest of which rulers?
accepted.x: Madhava Varma II acquired the title Trikuta-Malayadhipati after defeating the Anandagotrikas. Trikuta was identified with Kotappakonda in Guntur.
accepted.tq: Connect a victory-based title with the defeated power.
accepted.sec: Titles → ruler (Janasraya, Trikuta-Malayadhipati)  [APPSC]

accepted.s:
Which of the following pairs is correctly matched?

1. Govinda Varma — Shadabhigna
2. Vikramendra Varma I — Mahakavi
3. Indrabhattaraka Varma — Satyasraya
4. Vikramendra Varma II — Parama Saugata

Select the correct answer using the code given below.
accepted.x: Govinda Varma was Shadabhigna, Vikramendra Varma I was Mahakavi, and Indrabhattaraka Varma bore the title Satyasraya. Parama Saugata belonged to Vikramendra Varma I, not Vikramendra Varma II.
accepted.tq: Separate titles of successive rulers; the swapped title is the false statement.
accepted.sec: Titles → ruler (Janasraya, Trikuta-Malayadhipati)  [APPSC]

accepted.s:
Match List-I with List-II:

List-I (Title)
 a. Trisamudradhipati
 b. Shadabhigna
 c. Paramamaheshwara
 d. Sakala Bhuvana Rakshabharanaikashraya

List-II (Ruler)
 i. Govinda Varma
 ii. Madhava Varma II
 iii. Indrabhattaraka Varma
 iv. Vikramendra Varma II

Select the correct answer using the code below.
accepted.x: Trisamudradhipati belonged to Madhava Varma II; Shadabhigna to Govinda Varma; Paramamaheshwara to Indrabhattaraka Varma; and Sakala Bhuvana Rakshabharanaikashraya to Vikramendra Varma II.
accepted.tq: Start from the sure title–ruler pairs and eliminate codes.
accepted.sec: Titles → ruler (Janasraya, Trikuta-Malayadhipati)  [APPSC]

accepted.s: Who is associated with the titles Mahakavi and Parama Saugata?
accepted.x: Vikramendra Varma I was associated with the titles Mahakavi and Parama Saugata.
accepted.tq: Identify the ruler through a paired set of distinctive titles.
accepted.sec: Titles → ruler (Janasraya, Trikuta-Malayadhipati)  [APPSC]

accepted.s: Which Vishnukundin ruler is described as the founder and as a Vakataka vassal?
accepted.x: Indravarma, who ruled from 358 to 370 CE, is described as the founder of the Vishnukundin dynasty and a Vakataka vassal.
accepted.tq: Use the founder–political status association rather than the name alone.
accepted.sec: Rulers - chronological order and contribution  [APPSC]

accepted.s:
Madhava Varma I is associated with which combination of achievements?

1. He ruled for 22 years.
2. He married a Vakataka princess.
3. He excavated caves at Undavalli, Bhairavakona and Mogalrajapuram.

Which of the statements given above are correct?
accepted.x: All three statements are correct. Madhava Varma I ruled for 22 years, married a Vakataka princess and was associated with the excavation of the listed caves.
accepted.tq: Confirm a ruler’s contribution through a cluster of biographical statements.
accepted.sec: Rulers - chronological order and contribution  [APPSC]

accepted.s: The construction of a vihara by Queen Paramabhattarika and the establishment of Govinda Vihara at Chaitanyapuri are associated with which ruler?
accepted.x: These activities are associated with Govinda Varma I, whose rule also saw expansion into the Krishna-Godavari region and both sides of Sriparvata.
accepted.tq: Identify the ruler from associated religious and architectural activity.
accepted.sec: Rulers - chronological order and contribution  [APPSC]

accepted.s: Which ruler is regarded as the greatest Vishnukundin monarch and is associated with the golden age and Vedic revival?
accepted.x: Madhava Varma II is described as the greatest Vishnukundin ruler. His reign is associated with a golden age and Vedic revival.
accepted.tq: Match the evaluative description with the correct ruler.
accepted.sec: Rulers - chronological order and contribution  [APPSC]

accepted.s:
Consider the following statements:
1. Vikramendra Varma I was the son of Madhava Varma II by a Vakataka princess.
2. Indrabhattaraka Varma was defeated by Maukhari Ishanavarma.
3. Indrabhattaraka Varma was killed in the Kalinga war.
Which of the statements given above are correct?
accepted.x: All three statements are correct. Vikramendra Varma I was the son of Madhava Varma II and a Vakataka princess, while Indrabhattaraka Varma was defeated by Ishanavarma and killed in the Kalinga war.
accepted.tq: Combine dynastic relationship with military events and eliminate the partial combinations.
accepted.sec: Rulers - chronological order and contribution  [APPSC]

accepted.s:
Which of the following is correctly matched?

1. Indrabhattaraka Varma — Ghatikas
2. Vikramendra Varma II — Chikkulla, Tundi and second Tummalagudem plates
3. Manchana Bhattaraka — Last ruler

Select the correct answer using the code given below.
accepted.x: All three pairs are correct. Indrabhattaraka Varma was associated with Ghatikas, Vikramendra Varma II with the listed plates and suppression of revolts, and Manchana Bhattaraka was the last ruler.
accepted.tq: Verify multiple ruler–contribution pairs before selecting the complete combination.
accepted.sec: Rulers - chronological order and contribution  [APPSC]

accepted.s: According to the chronology given for the main Vishnukundin rulers, who succeeded Indravarma?
accepted.x: Indravarma was followed by Madhava Varma I, who ruled from 370 to 398 CE.
accepted.tq: Use immediate succession rather than attempting the whole sequence.
accepted.sec: Rulers - chronological order and contribution  [APPSC]

accepted.s: The Vishnukundin dynasty is dated as 358–569 CE by which chronological tradition mentioned for the dynasty?
accepted.x: APP places the Vishnukundin dynasty between 358 and 569 CE. CDX and APHQ give a different range, approximately 420–624 CE.
accepted.tq: Distinguish competing chronological ranges without merging them.
accepted.sec: Rulers - chronological order and contribution  [APPSC]

accepted.s: Which dynasty was formed by former Ikshvaku feudatories north of the Krishna and took its name from a gotra?
accepted.x: The Brihatpalayanas were former Ikshvaku feudatories north of the Krishna, and their name was derived from a gotra.
accepted.tq: Identify a dynasty from its political status and name origin.
accepted.sec: Sequence of post-Ikshvaku dynasties - correct order Ikshvakus → Brihatpalayanas → Salankayanas → Vishnukundins  [APPSC]

accepted.s: Which statement regarding the Brihatpalayanas is correct?
o: They followed Vaishnavism and had Vengi as their capital.
They were founded by Indravarma after the southern campaign of Samudragupta.
They ruled only the coastal region south of the Krishna.
Their only known king was Jayavarma, described as Brahmanical and Maheshwara-pada-parigrahita.
accepted.x: Jayavarma is the only known Brihatpalayana king and is described as Brahmanical and Maheshwara-pada-parigrahita.
accepted.tq: Select the precise dynasty profile while rejecting facts belonging to neighbouring dynasties.
accepted.sec: Sequence of post-Ikshvaku dynasties - correct order Ikshvakus → Brihatpalayanas → Salankayanas → Vishnukundins  [APPSC]

accepted.s:
Which of the following statements about the Salankayanas is correct?

1. Their capital was Vengi, identified with Pedavegi in Eluru district.
2. They followed Vaishnavism.
3. They were conquered by Madhava Varma II.

Select the correct answer using the code given below.
accepted.x: All three statements are correct. The Salankayana capital was Vengi or Pedavegi, they followed Vaishnavism, and Madhava Varma II conquered them.
accepted.tq: Test a dynasty through capital, religious affiliation and political fate.
accepted.sec: Sequence of post-Ikshvaku dynasties - correct order Ikshvakus → Brihatpalayanas → Salankayanas → Vishnukundins  [APPSC]

accepted.s: The rise of the Vishnukundins followed which development in the Deccan and Andhra region?
o: The Salankayanas established a new empire in Telangana.
Samudragupta’s southern campaign weakened the Pallavas.
The Mauryas restored Ikshvaku rule in Vijayapuri.
The Pallavas strengthened their authority after defeating Samudragupta.
accepted.x: The Vishnukundins rose after Samudragupta’s southern campaign of 358 CE weakened the Pallavas.
accepted.tq: Identify the political cause preceding the rise of a dynasty.
accepted.sec: Sequence of post-Ikshvaku dynasties - correct order Ikshvakus → Brihatpalayanas → Salankayanas → Vishnukundins  [APPSC]

accepted.s:
Which of the following statements about the Anandagotrikas is correct?

1. They were also former Ikshvaku feudatories.
2. Their capital was Kandarapuram.
3. They are associated with the Chejerla inscription.

Select the correct answer using the code given below.
accepted.x: All three statements are correct. The Anandagotrikas, also called the Kandara kings, were former Ikshvaku feudatories with Kandarapuram as their capital and are associated with the Chejerla inscription.
accepted.tq: Group related facts about a lesser-known neighbouring dynasty.
accepted.sec: Sequence of post-Ikshvaku dynasties - correct order Ikshvakus → Brihatpalayanas → Salankayanas → Vishnukundins  [APPSC]

accepted.s: Most historians regard the Vishnukundins as belonging to which social group?
o: Only hereditary feudatories of the Pallavas
accepted.x: Most historians regard the Vishnukundins as Brahmins belonging to the Vishnukundina gotra, although alternative caste theories have also been proposed.
accepted.tq: Identify the mainstream interpretation while distinguishing it from alternative theories.
accepted.sec: Origin debate - identification of Vishnukundi, original home

accepted.s:
Match the scholar with the theory attributed to him:

List-I (Scholar)
 a. B.V. Krishna Rao
 b. K. Gopalachari
 c. N. Venkataramanayya

List-II (Theory)
 i. Agnikula Kshatriyas
 ii. Brahmins
 iii. Brahmins who adopted Kshatriya ways

Select the correct answer using the code below.
accepted.x: B.V. Krishna Rao regarded them as Brahmins; K. Gopalachari proposed an Agnikula Kshatriya origin; N. Venkataramanayya described them as Brahmins who adopted Kshatriya ways.
accepted.tq: Start with the distinctive scholar–theory pair and complete the matching code.
accepted.sec: Origin debate - identification of Vishnukundi, original home

accepted.s: The name ‘Vishnukundi’ is generally identified with which place?
accepted.x: The name Vishnukundi is identified with Vinukonda in Guntur district, which is also listed among the Vishnukundin capitals.
accepted.tq: Distinguish the dynastic name’s geographical identification from its later territorial centres.
accepted.sec: Origin debate - identification of Vishnukundi, original home

accepted.s: Which region is indicated by the early records and forts as the original home of the Vishnukundins?
o: Telangana, including Amrabad, Keesaragutta and Indrapalanagara
The Krishna-Godavari coast after the Pallava wars
The coastal delta around Vengi alone
The southern Tamil region around Kandarapuram
accepted.x: Early records and forts at Amrabad, Keesaragutta and Indrapalanagara point to Telangana as the original home. The Vishnukundins later expanded into coastal Andhra.
accepted.tq: Infer the original homeland from the distribution of early forts and records.
accepted.sec: Origin debate - identification of Vishnukundi, original home

accepted.s: According to the stated political expansion, the Vishnukundins first ruled which region before expanding towards coastal Andhra?
o: The Kalinga coast under the Pallavas
The Vengi region under the Salankayanas
The area south of the Krishna around Vijayapuri
accepted.x: The Vishnukundins first ruled Telangana north of the Krishna and subsequently expanded into coastal Andhra.
accepted.tq: Use the direction of territorial expansion to identify the initial core region.
accepted.sec: Origin debate - identification of Vishnukundi, original home
